title: 2008 financial crisis
fact: The financial crisis and recession involved severe declines in asset prices and household wealth.
interpretation: Credit and equity losses can overwhelm a portfolio's government-rate hedge; funding and counterparty risks may dominate linear exposures.
limitation: Qualitative analogy only. No historical return series or calibrated replay is provided.
source_title: Federal Reserve History — The Great Recession

title: March 2020 market stress
fact: On March 23, 2020, the Federal Reserve announced Treasury and agency MBS purchases to support market functioning.
interpretation: Even assets used as hedges may face liquidity pressure. Margin needs and execution costs can matter more than first-order sensitivity.
limitation: Policy action is historical fact; the application to this synthetic portfolio is interpretation, not a measured backtest.

title: 2022 inflation / rates shock
fact: In December 2022, the Federal Reserve described elevated inflation and raised its target range to 4.25–4.50 percent.
interpretation: Inflation can drive government rates higher while pressuring credit and equity valuations, weakening conventional stock-bond diversification.
limitation: Qualitative regime comparison. Scenario shocks are illustrative assumptions, not 2022 observations.
